A long time after Musa (peace be upon him), an enemy defeated the Children of Israel. It drove them out of their homes and separated them from their children.

So their leaders came to a prophet who lived among them and said to him: ﴿ابْعَثْ لَنَا مَلِكًا نُّقَاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾

Their prophet said to them: ﴿هَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ إِن كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِتَالُ أَلَّا تُقَاتِلُوا﴾

He knew that talking is easy, but standing in front of the enemy is hard.

They said: ﴿وَمَا لَنَا أَلَّا نُقَاتِلَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَقَدْ أُخْرِجْنَا مِن دِيَارِنَا وَأَبْنَائِنَا﴾

He said to them: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ بَعَثَ لَكُمْ طَالُوتَ مَلِكًا﴾

They were surprised and said, "How can he be king over us when he doesn't have much money?"

He said: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفَاهُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَزَادَهُ بَسْطَةً فِي الْعِلْمِ وَالْجِسْمِ﴾

A leader needs knowledge and strength, not money.

Talut set out with the soldiers on a hot day. The road was long, and they grew more and more thirsty.

When they came near a river, he said to them: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ مُبْتَلِيكُم بِنَهَرٍ فَمَن شَرِبَ مِنْهُ فَلَيْسَ مِنِّي وَمَن لَّمْ يَطْعَمْهُ فَإِنَّهُ مِنِّي إِلَّا مَنِ اغْتَرَفَ غُرْفَةً بِيَدِهِ﴾

When they reached the water, most of them rushed to it and drank until they were full.

﴿فَشَرِبُوا مِنْهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِّنْهُمْ﴾

But a few of them took just one handful of water in their hand, then stood up and left the river.

If someone cannot be patient about a drink of water, how will he be patient in front of the enemy?

Talut crossed the river with the few who had been patient. When they saw the army of Jalut (Goliath), they saw more soldiers than anyone could count, and among them Jalut, a huge man wearing iron armor.

Some of them said: ﴿لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا الْيَوْمَ بِجَالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِ﴾

Then those who knew they would meet Allah stood up and said to their brothers:

﴿كَم مِّن فِئَةٍ قَلِيلَةٍ غَلَبَتْ فِئَةً كَثِيرَةً بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ ۗ وَاللَّهُ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾

Victory is not counted by heads; it comes from Allah.

When they went out to face Jalut and his soldiers, they did not ask for weapons first. Instead, they raised their hands to Allah:

﴿رَبَّنَا أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنَا صَبْرًا وَثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَنَا وَانصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾

They asked for patience before victory, and for steady feet before winning.

Then Jalut came out, calling for someone to fight him one on one. The scholars of tafsir say that Dawud (peace be upon him) was a young man in Talut's army that day. He had a sling and some stones. He threw a stone at Jalut, and Jalut fell.

﴿فَهَزَمُوهُم بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ وَقَتَلَ دَاوُودُ جَالُوتَ﴾

After that, Allah gave Dawud kingship and prophethood, and the people returned to their homes and their children.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ النَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍ لَّفَسَدَتِ الْأَرْضُ﴾

If the people of truth did not push back the wrongdoers, wrongdoing would fill the earth.

📖 Their story is in Surat Al-Baqarah, verses 246–251.
